text.description: Reach the Evolution Meadow area via the John Muir Trail, then climb the broad west-face gully to the north ridge and follow it to the top. Rock is loose; exit the gully to the south after the second tower to avoid class 3.

text.description: Hike up toward Armstrong Pass, join the Tahoe Rim Trail, and follow the Freel Peak trail up the sandy ridge to the summit. Several trail approaches exist, all non-technical.

name: Via Grouse Lake and Northwest Ridge

text.description: Follow the Copper Creek Trail to the Granite Basin area, then go cross-country to Grouse Lake. Climb to the saddle between Munger Peak and Goat, then follow the northwest ridge to the summit. Long day with a lot of gain.

text.description: Climb the Taboose Pass trail, go into the basin left of the summit ridge, and reach the saddle between Goodale and Striped Mountains. Scramble the steep slope to the southern pinnacle; only the last 20 ft are third class. Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 3.

name: Granite Chief Trail from Olympic Valley

text.description: Take the trail from behind the fire station along the ski area boundary to the Pacific Crest Trail, then follow the northeast ridge to the summit.
Follow the Pacific Crest Trail to Noble Lake, then a use trail to the saddle and class 2 sand to the summits.
Cross the San Joaquin River and take the Mammoth Trail and Beck Lakes Trail to Fern Lake, then climb scree to the ridge and the summit pyramid. About 7 miles each way, partly off-trail.

text.description: A long, mostly trail approach through the Kern Plateau meadows leads to a gentle cross-country finish up the east face. Sandy trail sections can be hard to follow.

name: Via Parker Pass and Koip Peak Pass

text.description: Follow the Mono Pass trail to the Parker Pass junction, cross Parker Pass, and climb switchbacks on Parker Peak's north flank to Koip Peak Pass. From there, a short walk-up over talus leads to the summit.

text.description: A short, steep trail climbs the ridge from the Canebrake Road saddle, fades in places, then follows cairns up the final ridge to the summit rocks. Expect a bit of scrambling and boulder hopping near the top.

text.description: Follow the PCT south from Sonora Pass, leave it at a notch on the ridge, and continue up the talus ridge to the broad summit area.
